Given there is no actual data we can use to compare brands on failure rate one of the ways you can do something close to a proxy of this is to just go look at reviews:

As you can see Razer gets about 75% 5/5 vs the CoolerMaster board with 62% 5/5.

I have been wanting to get into boxing for a while. My problem is money. I just don't have $150 to spend every month on lessons. I've taken advantage of a couple of free classes here and there, and I've learned some of the basics in footwork and various punches in combination with footwork. A set of gloves/wraps that came with a heavy bag, weighted jump rope, dumbbells up to 70 lbs each, pull up bar, and one adjustable resistance band.

A very simple boxing routine for beginners:

  1. Warm up stretching (5-10 min)
  2. Jump Rope (3 sets; 3 min with 1 min rest in-between)
  3. Work on foot work (3 sets…)(forward/backwards, left/right, mix it up etc., guard up)
  4. Shadow Box (3 sets…) (with hand wraps)
  5. Heavy bag (3 sets…) (with gloves)
  6. Jump Rope (3 sets…)
  7. Stretches (8-15+min)

This is just to get you started. I’m not sure how your conditioning is so you can adjust anything you think is necessary.

On 3-5 is where you can really focus on technique, it would be kind of hard to explain everything but if you wish I can offer input/suggestions/corrections if you post videos or if you have any questions feel free to ask.

P.s when you shadow box and hit the heavy bag, imagine that you are fighting. There are multiple videos on YouTube on how to defend against each punch, practice them when shadowboxing, etc…
